1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line and letter spacing in headings, labels, and body text.

2.why: Instructions are sentence-case with no italics or dense paragraphs; all-caps appears only in the 'NORTHSTAR BANK' and 'SECURITY CENTRE' branding labels, not in instructions.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centered column with large full-width buttons that suits mobile, though the ever-growing Logs panel makes later screens very long.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences (e.g., 'Enter the six-digit code generated during setup'), with only mild jargon such as 'MFA' and 'time-based'.

5.why: Placeholder examples show the expected format for the mobile number ('+15551234567') and recovery code ('ABCD-EFGH-JKLM'), though the code-entry fields rely on labels rather than worked examples.

6.why: No step requires reading a long passage; the longest required text is the three-line demo notice and all other messages are one to two lines.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are displayed as plain text with no copy or download control, and the UI explicitly instructs the user to 'add it manually' and 'Enter it manually'.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent (e.g., otpauth link) is offered on any screen; authenticator provisioning is manual-secret-only.

9.why: Fields are ordinary text inputs with no visible autocomplete or one-time-code hints and there is no password field, so autofill and password-manager support can neither be confirmed nor denied from the screenshots.

10.why: Every step opens with a large bold heading naming the task and a single solid-blue primary button that clearly dominates the page.

11.why: The enrolment steps ask for one action each, but the sign-in screen combines three fields with two buttons ('Verify and continue' and 'Get a simulation challenge') and the MFA settings page presents several actions at once.

12.why: Some actions produce clear inline banners ('Setup secret generated', 'Enrolment confirmed'), but others, such as the sent identity challenge and the accepted recovery code, are confirmed only by a line in the Logs panel.

13.why: 'Back to setup' links and re-request buttons exist, but there are no reveal/hide toggles for codes, and re-requesting backup codes permanently invalidates all previous codes as the warning banner states.

14.why: No error message appears in any of the 14 screens, so whether errors state the problem and fix without blame cannot be verified.

15.why: The UI itself describes the identity challenge as 'short-lived' and the authenticator codes as 'time-based', contradicting the claim of generous entry time, although no countdown timer pressures reading.
